audit_status.source_base: Greek Galatians text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Jerusalem meeting, Titus not compelled, right hand of fellowship, Cephas confrontation, justification/making-right by trust/faithfulness, crucified with Messiah.

verses.restored: Then after fourteen years I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, taking Titus along also.

familiar.text: Then fourteen years after I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and took Titus with me also.

modern.text: Fourteen years later I went up again to Jerusalem, accompanied by Barnabas. I took Titus along also.

original.text: Ἔπειτα διὰ δεκατεσσάρων ἐτῶν πάλιν ἀνέβην εἰς Ἱεροσόλυμα μετὰ Βαρναβᾶ συμπαραλαβὼν καὶ Τίτον·

verses.restored: I went up according to unveiling, and set before them the good news that I proclaim among the nations, privately to those seeming to be something, lest somehow I might be running or had run into emptiness.

familiar.text: And I went up by revelation, and communicated unto them that gospel which I preach among the Gentiles, but privately to them which were of reputation, lest by any means I should run, or had run, in vain.

modern.text: I went in response to a revelation and set before them the gospel that I preach among the Gentiles. But I spoke privately to those recognized as leaders, for fear that I was running or had already run in vain.

original.text: ἀνέβην δὲ κατὰ ἀποκάλυψιν· καὶ ἀνεθέμην αὐτοῖς τὸ εὐαγγέλιον ὃ κηρύσσω ἐν τοῖς ἔθνεσιν, κατʼ ἰδίαν δὲ τοῖς δοκοῦσιν, μή πως εἰς κενὸν τρέχω ἢ ἔδραμον.

verses.restored: But not even Titus, who was with me, being Greek, was compelled to be circumcised.

familiar.text: But neither Titus, who was with me, being a Greek, was compelled to be circumcised:

modern.text: Yet not even Titus, who was with me, was compelled to be circumcised, even though he was a Greek.

original.text: ἀλλʼ οὐδὲ Τίτος ὁ σὺν ἐμοί, Ἕλλην ὤν, ἠναγκάσθη περιτμηθῆναι·

verses.restored: But because of false siblings secretly brought in, who slipped in to spy out our freedom that we have in Messiah Jesus, so that they might enslave us,

familiar.text: And that because of false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage:

modern.text: This issue arose because some false brothers had come in under false pretenses to spy on our freedom in Christ Jesus, in order to enslave us.

original.text: διὰ δὲ τοὺς παρεισάκτους ψευδαδέλφους, οἵτινες παρεισῆλθον κατασκοπῆσαι τὴν ἐλευθερίαν ἡμῶν ἣν ἔχομεν ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ, ἵνα ἡμᾶς ⸀καταδουλώσουσιν—

verses.restored: to whom we yielded in submission not even for an hour, so that the truth of the good news might remain with you.

familiar.text: To whom we gave place by subjection, no, not for an hour; that the truth of the gospel might continue with you.

modern.text: We did not give in to them for a moment, so that the truth of the gospel would remain with you.

original.text: οἷς οὐδὲ πρὸς ὥραν εἴξαμεν τῇ ὑποταγῇ, ἵνα ἡ ἀλήθεια τοῦ εὐαγγελίου διαμείνῃ πρὸς ὑμᾶς.

verses.restored: But from those seeming to be something, whatever they once were makes no difference to me; the Divine takes no human face; for those seeming added nothing to me.

familiar.text: But of these who seemed to be somewhat, (whatsoever they were, it maketh no matter to me: God accepteth no man’s person:) for they who seemed to be somewhat in conference added nothing to me:

modern.text: But as for the highly esteemed—whatever they were makes no difference to me; God does not show favoritism —those leaders added nothing to me.

original.text: ἀπὸ δὲ τῶν δοκούντων εἶναί τι— ὁποῖοί ποτε ἦσαν οὐδέν μοι διαφέρει· πρόσωπον ⸀θεὸς ἀνθρώπου οὐ λαμβάνει— ἐμοὶ γὰρ οἱ δοκοῦντες οὐδὲν προσανέθεντο,

verses.restored: But on the contrary, seeing that I had been entrusted with the good news of the uncircumcision, just as Peter of the circumcision,

familiar.text: But contrariwise, when they saw that the gospel of the uncircumcision was committed unto me, as the gospel of the circumcision was unto Peter;

modern.text: On the contrary, they saw that I had been entrusted to preach the gospel to the uncircumcised, just as Peter had been to the circumcised.

original.text: ἀλλὰ τοὐναντίον ἰδόντες ὅτι πεπίστευμαι τὸ εὐαγγέλιον τῆς ἀκροβυστίας καθὼς Πέτρος τῆς περιτομῆς,

verses.restored: for the One working in Peter for apostleship of the circumcision worked also in me for the nations,

familiar.text: (For he that wrought effectually in Peter to the apostleship of the circumcision, the same was mighty in me toward the Gentiles:)

modern.text: For the One who was at work in Peter’s apostleship to the circumcised was also at work in my apostleship to the Gentiles.

original.text: ὁ γὰρ ἐνεργήσας Πέτρῳ εἰς ἀποστολὴν τῆς περιτομῆς ἐνήργησεν καὶ ἐμοὶ εἰς τὰ ἔθνη,

verses.restored: and knowing the grace given to me, James and Cephas and John, those seeming to be pillars, gave to me and Barnabas right hands of fellowship/participation, that we should go to the nations and they to the circumcision.

familiar.text: And when James, Cephas, and John, who seemed to be pillars, perceived the grace that was given unto me, they gave to me and Barnabas the right hands of fellowship; that we should go unto the heathen, and they unto the circumcision.

modern.text: And recognizing the grace that I had been given, James, Cephas, and John—those reputed to be pillars—gave me and Barnabas the right hand of fellowship, so that we should go to the Gentiles, and they to the circumcised.

original.text: καὶ γνόντες τὴν χάριν τὴν δοθεῖσάν μοι, Ἰάκωβος καὶ Κηφᾶς καὶ Ἰωάννης, οἱ δοκοῦντες στῦλοι εἶναι, δεξιὰς ἔδωκαν ἐμοὶ καὶ Βαρναβᾷ κοινωνίας, ἵνα ⸀ἡμεῖς εἰς τὰ ἔθνη, αὐτοὶ δὲ εἰς τὴν περιτομήν·

verses.restored: Only that we remember the poor, which very thing I was eager to do.

familiar.text: Only they would that we should remember the poor; the same which I also was forward to do.

modern.text: They only asked us to remember the poor, the very thing I was eager to do. Paul Confronts Cephas

original.text: μόνον τῶν πτωχῶν ἵνα μνημονεύωμεν, ὃ καὶ ἐσπούδασα αὐτὸ τοῦτο ποιῆσαι.

verses.restored: But when Cephas came to Antioch, I opposed him to his face, because he stood condemned.

familiar.text: But when Peter was come to Antioch, I withstood him to the face, because he was to be blamed.

modern.text: When Cephas came to Antioch, however, I opposed him to his face, because he stood to be condemned.

original.text: Ὅτε δὲ ἦλθεν ⸀Κηφᾶς εἰς Ἀντιόχειαν, κατὰ πρόσωπον αὐτῷ ἀντέστην, ὅτι κατεγνωσμένος ἦν·

verses.restored: For before certain ones came from James, he was eating with the nations; but when they came, he drew back and separated himself, fearing those from the circumcision.

familiar.text: For before that certain came from James, he did eat with the Gentiles: but when they were come, he withdrew and separated himself, fearing them which were of the circumcision.

modern.text: For before certain men came from James, he used to eat with the Gentiles. But when they arrived, he began to draw back and separate himself, for fear of those in the circumcision group.

original.text: πρὸ τοῦ γὰρ ἐλθεῖν τινας ἀπὸ Ἰακώβου μετὰ τῶν ἐθνῶν συνήσθιεν· ὅτε δὲ ⸀ἦλθον, ὑπέστελλεν καὶ ἀφώριζεν ἑαυτόν, φοβούμενος τοὺς ἐκ περιτομῆς.

verses.restored: And the rest of the Judeans joined him in hypocrisy, so that even Barnabas was carried away by their hypocrisy.

familiar.text: And the other Jews dissembled likewise with him; insomuch that Barnabas also was carried away with their dissimulation.

modern.text: The other Jews joined him in his hypocrisy, so that by their hypocrisy even Barnabas was led astray.

original.text: καὶ συνυπεκρίθησαν αὐτῷ ⸀καὶ οἱ λοιποὶ Ἰουδαῖοι, ὥστε καὶ Βαρναβᾶς συναπήχθη αὐτῶν τῇ ὑποκρίσει.

verses.restored: But when I saw that they were not walking straight toward the truth of the good news, I said to Cephas before all: If you, being Judean, live like the nations and not like Judean, how do you compel the nations to Judaize?

familiar.text: But when I saw that they walked not uprightly according to the truth of the gospel, I said unto Peter before them all, If thou, being a Jew, livest after the manner of Gentiles, and not as do the Jews, why compellest thou the Gentiles to live as do the Jews?

modern.text: When I saw that they were not walking in line with the truth of the gospel, I said to Cephas in front of them all, “If you, who are a Jew, live like a Gentile and not like a Jew, how can you compel the Gentiles to live like Jews?”

original.text: ἀλλʼ ὅτε εἶδον ὅτι οὐκ ὀρθοποδοῦσιν πρὸς τὴν ἀλήθειαν τοῦ εὐαγγελίου, εἶπον τῷ ⸀Κηφᾷ ἔμπροσθεν πάντων· Εἰ σὺ Ἰουδαῖος ὑπάρχων ἐθνικῶς ⸂καὶ ⸀οὐκ Ἰουδαϊκῶς ζῇς⸃, ⸀πῶς τὰ ἔθνη ἀναγκάζεις Ἰουδαΐζειν;

verses.restored: We, by nature Judeans and not sinners from the nations,

familiar.text: We who are Jews by nature, and not sinners of the Gentiles,

modern.text: We who are Jews by birth and not Gentile “sinners”

original.text: Ἡμεῖς φύσει Ἰουδαῖοι καὶ οὐκ ἐξ ἐθνῶν ἁμαρτωλοί,

verses.restored: yet knowing that a human is not made righteous/just from works of Law but through trust/faithfulness of Jesus Messiah, even we trusted into Messiah Jesus, so that we might be made righteous/just from trust/faithfulness of Messiah and not from works of Law, because from works of Law no flesh will be made righteous/just.

familiar.text: Knowing that a man is not justified by the works of the law, but by the faith of Jesus Christ, even we have believed in Jesus Christ, that we might be justified by the faith of Christ, and not by the works of the law: for by the works of the law shall no flesh be justified.

modern.text: know that a man is not justified by works of the law, but by faith in Jesus Christ. So we, too, have believed in Christ Jesus, that we may be justified by faith in Christ and not by works of the law, because by works of the law no one will be justified.

original.text: εἰδότες ⸀δὲ ὅτι οὐ δικαιοῦται ἄνθρωπος ἐξ ἔργων νόμου ἐὰν μὴ διὰ πίστεως ⸂Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ⸃, καὶ ἡμεῖς εἰς Χριστὸν Ἰησοῦν ἐπιστεύσαμεν, ἵνα δικαιωθῶμεν ἐκ πίστεως Χριστοῦ καὶ οὐκ ἐξ ἔργων νόμου, ⸂ὅτι ἐξ ἔργων νόμου οὐ δικαιωθήσεται⸃ πᾶσα σάρξ.

verses.restored: But if, seeking to be made righteous/just in Messiah, we ourselves also were found sinners/misaligned, is Messiah then servant of sin/misalignment? May it not be.

familiar.text: But if, while we seek to be justified by Christ, we ourselves also are found sinners, is therefore Christ the minister of sin? God forbid.

modern.text: But if, while we seek to be justified in Christ, we ourselves are found to be sinners, does that make Christ a minister of sin? Certainly not!

original.text: εἰ δὲ ζητοῦντες δικαιωθῆναι ἐν Χριστῷ εὑρέθημεν καὶ αὐτοὶ ἁμαρτωλοί, ἆρα Χριστὸς ἁμαρτίας διάκονος; μὴ γένοιτο·

verses.restored: For if what I tore down, these things I build again, I show myself a transgressor.

familiar.text: For if I build again the things which I destroyed, I make myself a transgressor.

modern.text: If I rebuild what I have already torn down, I prove myself to be a lawbreaker.

original.text: εἰ γὰρ ἃ κατέλυσα ταῦτα πάλιν οἰκοδομῶ, παραβάτην ἐμαυτὸν ⸀συνιστάνω.

verses.restored: For through Law I died to Law, so that I might live to the Divine.

familiar.text: For I through the law am dead to the law, that I might live unto God.

modern.text: For through the law I died to the law so that I might live to God.

original.text: ἐγὼ γὰρ διὰ νόμου νόμῳ ἀπέθανον ἵνα θεῷ ζήσω· Χριστῷ συνεσταύρωμαι·

verses.restored: I have been crucified with Messiah; and I no longer live, but Messiah lives in me. And what I now live in flesh, I live in trust, the trust/faithfulness of the Son of the Divine, who loved me and gave himself for me.

familiar.text: I am crucified with Christ: nevertheless I live; yet not I, but Christ liveth in me: and the life which I now live in the flesh I live by the faith of the Son of God, who loved me, and gave himself for me.

modern.text: I have been crucified with Christ, and I no longer live, but Christ lives in me. The life I live in the body, I live by faith in the Son of God, who loved me and gave Himself up for me.

original.text: ζῶ δὲ οὐκέτι ἐγώ, ζῇ δὲ ἐν ἐμοὶ Χριστός· ὃ δὲ νῦν ζῶ ἐν σαρκί, ἐν πίστει ζῶ τῇ τοῦ ⸂υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ⸃ τοῦ ἀγαπήσαντός με καὶ παραδόντος ἑαυτὸν ὑπὲρ ἐμοῦ.

verses.restored: I do not set aside the grace of the Divine; for if righteousness/justice is through Law, then Messiah died freely/for nothing.

familiar.text: I do not frustrate the grace of God: for if righteousness come by the law, then Christ is dead in vain.

modern.text: I do not set aside the grace of God. For if righteousness comes through the law, Christ died for nothing.

original.text: οὐκ ἀθετῶ τὴν χάριν τοῦ θεοῦ· εἰ γὰρ διὰ νόμου δικαιοσύνη, ἄρα Χριστὸς δωρεὰν ἀπέθανεν.

translation_notes: Works of Law should be read in the Galatians context as boundary/covenant practices pressed on nations, not as a generic attack on all good works.
Pistis Christou in verses 16 and 20 is preserved with trust/faithfulness ambiguity, allowing both Messiah's faithfulness and human trust-response.
Cephas confrontation is an intra-apostolic dispute over table fellowship and Gentile inclusion, not anti-Jewish polemic.
